**CC — THE 100-DOMAIN LIMIT IS A METHOD ERROR, NOT A CEILING. Alex 2026-08-27: "that limit is an error in method I think — we are on CF for SaaS paid, how can it be."**

**He is right and this needs checking before anyone asks for a limit raise.** Two different Cloudflare features are being confused, and we are almost certainly using the wrong one:

**1. WORKERS CUSTOM DOMAINS** — attaching a hostname directly to a Worker, one entry per hostname. **This is what has a ~100 limit and what we have filled up.** It was never meant for a platform spawning subdomains per app.
**2. CLOUDFLARE FOR SaaS / CUSTOM HOSTNAMES** — built for exactly our case: a platform serving many hostnames, scaling to thousands, priced per hostname. **If we are paying for CF for SaaS, we should be using this and we are not.**

**AND FOR OUR OWN SUBDOMAINS THERE IS A SIMPLER ANSWER THAN EITHER:**
**A WILDCARD WORKERS ROUTE — `*.abilifi.net/*` — ONE ENTRY, UNLIMITED SUBDOMAINS.** Every app we host on our own zone resolves through it. **No per-app registration, no limit, nothing to top up.**
That also lands the tenancy ruling for free (m65556): **the host resolves to an instance, the instance to an org.** A wildcard route is the natural implementation of that — **one route, and the subdomain itself carries the tenancy.** Registering each app individually was always going to fight that model.

**SO, IN ORDER:**
1. **CONFIRM WHICH FEATURE THE 100 ENTRIES ARE** — Workers Custom Domains or SaaS Custom Hostnames. Read the account, do not infer.
2. **CONFIRM WHAT CF FOR SaaS WE ACTUALLY PAY FOR**, and whether custom hostnames are available on it.
3. **MOVE OUR OWN APPS TO A WILDCARD ROUTE** on abilifi.net — nano-banana, substack and anything on workers.dev come home, and the ledger and updates routes stop being individual buttons for Alex.
4. **RESERVE CUSTOM HOSTNAMES FOR CUSTOMER-OWNED DOMAINS ONLY** — a client pointing their own domain at us. That is what the feature is for and what we pay for.

**DO

**CC — NEXT WORK IS THE AUDIT. INFRA AND FRAG DEPTH, IN THAT ORDER. Alex 2026-08-27: "audit CC's next work — prefer infra, frag depth."**

Not new features. **Depth on what exists.** Two passes, both read-only.

== 1. INFRA AUDIT — what we actually run, from the account, not from tickets ==
**Start with the domain question (65631)** — it is the live one and it blocks every new app:
- which feature the 100 entries are: Workers Custom Domains or SaaS Custom Hostnames
- what CF for SaaS we actually pay for
- **whether a wildcard `*.abilifi.net/*` route removes the ceiling entirely**
**Then the rest of the estate, same read-only discipline as Vultr and GridPane:**
- **every deployed worker**: what it is, what routes reach it, what bindings it holds, when it last deployed, **and whether anything calls it**. The BUILT/UNWIRED register exists for exactly this and today produced two more entries.
- **every D1, KV, R2 bucket, DO namespace, queue**: what writes it, what reads it, **what is orphaned**. The memplug root cause was *hundreds of per-frag D1s* nobody has counted — **count them, and say how many have no consumer.**
- **the 6 of 11 app-host surfaces returning 404** — which are real routes that broke, which are dead entries to delete.
- **spend**: what this estate costs per month, per service, real figures.
**A pass that changes what it measures cannot be trusted. Read only. A missing thing is a finding, not something to fix in passing.**

== 2. FRAG DEPTH — the 13-surface audit (65619, 65621) ==
Read-only graph query. Per frag: which of **frag · mcp · cli · text · help · big · full · mobile · activity · cue · social · changelog · cheer · kairos** it declares, **plus typed in/out yes or no.**
**And DEPTH means more than presence:** for each frag also report **how many spec docs exist for it** (2432 has five, 2427 has three, none canonical), **how many open SPEC_ASKs**, and **spec length vs frag length** — the standard approved today.
**If the graph holds none of this,

**CC — CONFIRMED: WE ARE ON WORKERS FOR PLATFORMS AND WE ARE NOT USING IT. THE 100-DOMAIN CEILING IS THE EXACT BOTTLENECK IT EXISTS TO REMOVE.** Alex 2026-08-27, verified against CF docs.

**THE LIMITS WE ARE HITTING ARE THE ORDINARY-WORKERS LIMITS:** *500 scripts per account, 1000 routes per zone, and 100 custom domains per zone — "which can become a bottleneck if you want to provide a dedicated Workers environment for each customer."* **That is us, word for word.**

**WHAT WORKERS FOR PLATFORMS GIVES, FROM CF'S OWN DOCS:**
- **UNLIMITED WORKERS — "no per-account script limits apply to Workers in a namespace."** So the 500-script ceiling goes too, not just the domains.
- **ONE DYNAMIC DISPATCH WORKER IS THE ENTRY POINT FOR ALL REQUESTS**, routing by hostname, path or headers.
- **HOSTNAME ROUTING IS THE DOCUMENTED PATTERN:** `const customerName = new URL(request.url).hostname.split(".")[0]; return env.DISPATCHER.get(customerName).fetch(request);`
- **"Host applications under a subdomain of your domain (customer-name.myplatform.com) or integrate with custom hostnames to allow customers to use their own domains."**
- Per-customer CPU and subrequest limits, tags, observability across all user workers.

**AND IT IS OUR TENANCY RULING IMPLEMENTED NATIVELY.** m65556: *the host resolves to an instance, the instance resolves to an org.* **That is literally the dispatch worker's job.** We specced it this afternoon and Cloudflare ships it — we have been hand-rolling a worse version by registering each app as its own custom domain.

**SO THE FIX IS NOT A WILDCARD ROUTE, IT IS A DISPATCH NAMESPACE:**
1. **CONFIRM WHAT WE ACTUALLY PAY FOR** — read the account. If WfP is on the plan, the ceiling is self-inflicted.
2. **CREATE A DISPATCH NAMESPACE** (dashboard supports it now — Compute & AI → Workers for Platforms).
3. **ONE DYNAMIC DISPATCH WORKER on `*.abilifi.net`**, routing hostname → user worker → org. **One route replaces 100 custom domains, and every future app needs none.

NEXT WORK = THE TWO AUDITS (65632), both READ-ONLY (Vultr/GridPane discipline — observe, never mutate), infra first:
[INFRA] agent: starts with the DOMAIN QUESTION (65631) from the ACCOUNT not inference — which feature the ~100 entries are (Workers Custom Domains vs CF-for-SaaS Custom Hostnames), what SaaS plan we pay for, and whether a wildcard *.abilifi.net/* route removes the ceiling entirely (one route, unlimited subdomains, lands host->instance->org tenancy for free). RECOMMENDS the wildcard move + reserve-custom-hostnames-for-customer-domains with exact steps, does NOT execute it (read-only pass). Then every worker (routes/bindings/last-deploy/who-calls = BUILT/UNWIRED orphans), every D1/KV/R2/DO/queue (COUNT the per-frag D1s + how many have NO consumer — the memplug root cause), the 6/11 404s (real vs dead-to-delete), monthly spend.
[FRAG DEPTH] agent: read-only graph query, per frag which of the 14 (frag·mcp·cli·text·help · big·full·mobile·activity·cue · social·changelog·cheer·kairos) + typed-in/out y/n, plus spec-docs-count, open spec_asks, spec-len-vs-frag-len. If the graph holds NO frag declarations, that is the headline — report + stop, no writing.
Both post real numbers or a NAMED unreadable-scope button; neither writes anything. Whole build wave before this = landed + committed; loop live + landing again post-memplug.

**CC — CLARIFICATION FROM ALEX ON 65635. THE FIX IS THE DISPATCH NAMESPACE. FRAGS ARE NOT SUBDOMAINS.** 2026-08-27: "why subdomains for frags — why not just a page under widgets.abilifi" → "the fix is dispatch namespace."

**I CONFLATED TWO LEVELS AND HE CORRECTED IT:**
- **A FRAG IS A CAPABILITY, NOT A DEPLOYMENT.** It renders at `widgets.abilifi.net/<frag>`. **A path. No DNS entry, no custom domain, no ceiling.**
- **A SUBDOMAIN IS FOR TENANCY**, because it is the one thing a path cannot express — `pathmos.abilifi.net` says which org owns the instance and scopes everything beneath it. **A path under widgets says nothing about who owns it.**
**TENANT → SUBDOMAIN. FRAG → PATH.** That is the rule and it removes most of the problem before the namespace is even involved.

**AND THE DISPATCH NAMESPACE IS THE FIX FOR WHAT REMAINS:**
- **ONE DYNAMIC DISPATCH WORKER on `*.abilifi.net`.** It reads the hostname's first label → resolves the tenant → dispatches. `env.DISPATCHER.get(name)`. **That is our host→instance→org ruling (m65556), implemented natively rather than hand-rolled.**
- **UNLIMITED WORKERS IN THE NAMESPACE** — no per-account script limit, no per-zone custom-domain limit. **One route replaces 100 entries and every future app needs zero.**
- Deploy with `wrangler deploy --dispatch-namespace <ns>`. Per-tenant CPU and subrequest limits, tags, observability across all user workers come with it.

**SO NANO-BANANA AND SUBSTACK ON workers.dev WERE THE WRONG SHAPE TWICE OVER** — registered as individual custom domains when they are either a PATH under an existing host or a WORKER IN THE NAMESPACE behind the dispatcher. **Neither needs its own DNS entry.**

**ORDER:**
1. Confirm WfP is on the account (we believe it is paid for).
2. Create the dispatch namespace.
3. **One dispatch worker on `*.abilifi.net`**, hostname → tenant → worker.
4. Move apps into the namespace; bring nano-banana and substack home off workers.dev.
5. **Frags render as PATHS under widgets.abilifi.n
